newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BT, Vodafone options busy as shares rise.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BT, Vodafone options busy as shares rise.

text.p: The UK stock options market was a frenzy of activity on Wednesday with traders taking advantage of a strong stock market in order to take positions in various stocks, dealers said.
Spreads and volatility trades accounted for the bulk of business in British Telecommunications and Vodafone -- companies in the telephone network sector.

One such deal in BT was a call spread established by selling of 1,000 May 420 calls at 33p and 1,000 May 460 calls at 12p for a net credit of 21p. Maximum profit at expiry will be 21p if BT shares go below 420p.
There was also a seller of 750 May 460 calls in BT at 14p.
By 1515 GMT, BT shares were up 13p at 443-1/2p. The company will announce third quarter results tomorrow.
For Vodafone the biggest deal was a long strangle created by buying 1,000 July 280 puts at 17p and 1,000 July 300 calls at 19p. Increased volatility will help this deal make money.
If the position is held to expiry a profit will be made if the shares either go below 244p or go above 336p.
In contrast, a short strangle was the main deal in supermarket chain Safeway.
The deal was to sell 1,000 April 360 puts in Safeway at 6-1/2p as well as 1,000 April 420 calls at 6-1/2p.
Over in pharmaceuticals group SmithKline Beecham was wanted in a hedging transaction.
The deal was to sell 1,050 April 800 puts at 11p to cover the sale of 200,000 shares at 866-1/2p. For profits to accrue by expiry, the shares price needs to fall below 800p.
